summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official: Ten-Minute Beginner Tutorial - Elastic Waistband Sports Pants ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to create elastic waistband sports pants using Marvelous Designer. Follow along as we go through the steps to design, sew, and simulate the garment. ## Setting Up the Basic Pants File From the library window, enter the basic pants file. After selecting the rectangle tool, click on the 2D window to input specific values. Press **Ctrl + D** to create a symmetrical version of the pants. ## Arranging the Belt Plate Show the arrangement point using **Shift + F** and arrange the belt plate. Use the line sewing tool to sew the belt. You can change its position by adjusting the various arrangement values in the attribute editor. ### Ensuring Proper Fit We need to ensure that the belt curve aligns with the human body curve. By contrast, you can see that the belt curve should follow the body's natural shape. The front of the pants is lower than the front of the belt. Add some curve points to draw a curve and modify the angle to a right angle. ## Adjusting and Simulating the Belt Press **Ctrl + D** and move the point along the curve to shorten the length of the upper and lower eyes. After simulation, you will see a belt that fits better to the body. Freeze the belt plate and use the free sewing tool to sew the plate. ### Creating Seam Lines After creating the first seam line, press **Shift + D** and continue to click on the line. Select the multi-line seam line to be sewn. Activate the belt plate and simulate. Then, select the edit seam line tool, choose the line in the back of the plate, and select the "merge" option in the menu in the right-hand corner. ## Belt Application Stitch For the belt application stitch, ensure that the stitch maintains the shape of the plate in the 2D window and does not slide easily. In the library, in the acceptable window, we can fold the hem of the pants and place them on the virtual model. Move the bottom of the pants to shorten their length. ## Creating the Foot Plate In the 3D window, freeze the belt plate. Since the belt is frozen, the pants will shrink upward after the application mirror shrink. Now we can create the foot plate. Select the rectangle and click on the 2D window, then enter specific values. ### Adjusting the Foot Plate Press **Ctrl + D** to create a symmetrical plate. Use the line sewing tool to sew the side of the foot plate, and you can drag the plate to adjust its position. The applied foot plate will maintain its shape and reduce the sliding of other plates. ### Detailing the Clothing Reducing the scale can increase the detail of the clothing, which helps to verify if the clothing is integrated properly. You can adjust the size of the foot plate. Use the free sewing tool to sew the foot plate to the pants plate. ## Controlling the Seam Length After creating the first seam line, press the **Shift** key and click on all the seams. The seam line will reduce to 100%. Adjust the length of the pants to control the fold by moving the line and entering specific values in the window. ### Setting Elastic Proportions To remove the symmetrical layer of the waist, set the proportion of the elastic application on the outer line of the upper and lower plates to 100. This step maintains the length of the line, ensuring the plate is not transformed by seam line impacts. ## Fixing the Waist Belt Position Select the waist belt line and the inner curve line, applying the same 100% proportion of elasticity for the middle line. To fix the waist belt position, press the **W** key and click on the clothing to add a fixed needle. Select the waist belt and the outer curve line, then cancel the stickiness and elasticity of the curve line on the plate. ### Removing Unneeded Joints Choose to remove the joint, canceling the joint of the inner and outer layers. Double-click to select the center point of the frame and activate it, allowing the center to be loosened on the plate. Delete any sewing line created by the Cologne layer and re-select the sewing plate using the free sewing tool. ## Adding Linked Lines Add a linked line to enable continuous tailoring. You can see how much has been reduced. After that, freeze the pants and waist belt plates. ### Adjusting Particle Diameter For smaller plates, reduce the particle diameter to achieve more detailed results. For the ankle plate, use 100% elasticity to keep its length unchanged. Select the ankle plate and the outer layer of the clavicle from the menu bar on the right. ## Final Adjustments After removing the joint of the ankle plate on the clavicle, cancel the elastic and banding applications. When the corresponding plates have no joint relationship, remove the joint for them. ### Creating the Pocket Next, let’s create the pocket. In the 3D window, select the 3D panel tool. Click on the panel to create a line. Press **CTRL** and click to create a curve point. Use the 3D panel tool to select the line drawn on the pants panel. ## Finalizing the Pocket In the menu in the right-hand corner, select "cut and sew" under the symmetrical column. Select the pocket panel's panel line, then choose "panel line expansion" and select "Extend" as the side angle. Once the panel is created, use the free sewing tool to sew up the part that was extended in the pocket. ### Adjusting the Version Don't forget to copy the adjustment of the agreed line and ensure precision. Use the tool to modify the curve of the version. Select the pants version and access the Cron from the outside in the menu bar on the right. ## Enhancing the Design Unlock the link and set the left and right symmetry of the original version of the Cron. Increase the aspect ratio and the tail ratio to make the outer version look larger than the inner version. After reducing the particle diameter, the spine will appear more detailed and smooth. ### Utilizing Pre-set Fabrics In the material file folder within the library, navigate to the fabric folder. Here, you can find the pre-set fabric in Marvelous Designer. Use the knit cotton jersey to dress the version. ## Working with Layer Masks Add a layer mask to the work area. You can learn how to create it through previous videos. Arrange the panels in the 2D window and set the layer level to 1 for the face mask. ### Final Simulation Freeze the pants panels to prevent wear and tear from becoming unstable. After placing the face mask on the outside of the pants, activate all panels and set the layer level to 0. Simulate to allow the panels to naturally wear on the model. ## Conclusion Open the project page to see if the model has changed. Select the model and click in the control panel to view the updates. Now, you can observe that the model is different from the original, having created a new 3D model that reflects your design. ```
